title: cost-optimization: autotune defaults for batching/caching, quantization profiles, and unit-econ tooling
author: Priya Patel
description:
Motivation: Customers consistently ask for better out-of-the-box cost/perf defaults and automated recommendations for inference settings. This PR bundles three coordinated changes: 1) autotune and improved defaults for batching and KV-prefetch caching, 2) quantization profile presets and automated selection hooks, and 3) unit-economics tooling to estimate per-request cost and recommended configs. The goal is a low-friction path to 20-40% token-cost reductions for common workloads while preserving latency SLOs.

What changed (high level):
- Runtime: added an autotuner that profiles request size/seq-length distributions and suggests batching/windowing parameters; includes safe rollback heuristics.
- Caching: improved default KV cache TTLs and prefix caching policies; added a small in-memory LRU for short-lived sessions to reduce cold-Attention recompute.
- Quantization: introduced three quant profiles (fp16, int8-dq, int8-gptq) with compatibility matrix for model families and a selection hook during model onboarding and routing.
- Tooling: unit-econ CLI and API (+console integration) that simulates per-token costs across configs, shows recommended profile, and surface expected savings.
- Docs/Examples: quickstart for enabling autotune on Dedicated/Private deployments and migration notes for existing pinned configs.

Checklist: 
- [x] Runtime autotuner prototype implemented
- [x] Quant profiles integrated with model registry and compatibility checks
- [x] Unit-econ simulator and initial console UI tiles
- [x] E2E canary + perf-run tests
- [x] Docs and customer-facing release notes

Testing & CI: ran unit tests, integration tests against perf-canary infra, and a 72-hour canary with internal traffic. Observed median cost-per-1000-tokens drop of ~28% on conversational workloads with identical prompt/response quality (BLEU/ROUGE stable within noise).

Rollout plan: feature gated behind account opt-in flag. Canary -> gradual 10% increments over 48h with automatic rollback on latency or quality regression triggers.

Related: Linear ENG-4821 (autotune design), ENG-4890 (unit-econ dashboards), and earlier PRs in this series (see pr-91321, pr-92400).

review_comments: Diego Morales: Can the autotuner respect user pinning at route level? Suggested adding an explicit opt-out flag per-route.
Priya Patel: Reply: added route-level opt-out and documented precedence. The autotuner will not override pinned configs; it only suggests defaults for unpinned routes.
Ava Chen: Request changes: quantify rollback thresholds and make them configurable. Also asked for additional telemetry metrics (per-config token cost).
Priya Patel: Reply: exposed rollback_threshold_ms and rollback_quality_delta in config and added cost telemetry. Included in tests and console panel.
Samir Gupta: Approved after verifying quant profile compatibility matrix and zero-downtime model swap behavior.
release_notes:
- Added autotune for batching and KV caching defaults to reduce per-token costs
- Introduced quantization profile presets (fp16, int8-dq, int8-gptq) and automated selection hooks
- Unit-economics simulator and console integration to estimate savings and recommend configs
- Opt-in rollout with safe rollback heuristics
